security_audit.summary: This skill provides two documented CLI tools for creating and updating Linear projects through the official Linear SDK. The static analyzer produced 37 findings, but nearly all are false positives: the 29 'Ruby/shell backtick execution' hits are Markdown code fences and inline-code backticks in the SKILL.md documentation, not code that executes commands; the network hit is a hardcoded link to the bun.sh documentation site; and the environment and sensitive-file findings refer to the legitimate, well-documented LINEAR_API_KEY that the tool requires to authenticate with Linear. The API key is read from the environment or a project .env file per standard practice and is not exfiltrated or logged. No prompt injection, data exfiltration, or business-logic abuse was observed.

remediation.issue: The skill instructs users to place LINEAR_API_KEY in a file at the git repository root (.env).
remediation.suggestion: Recommend that users add .env to .gitignore so the API key is never committed. Consider documenting an environment-variable-only option for CI or shared environments.

content.user_title: Create and Update Linear Projects from the CLI
content.value_statement: Managing Linear projects through the web interface is slow when you work in the terminal or automate workflows. This skill lets you create and update projects with simple commands, so you can manage project data directly from scripts and the command line.
actual_capabilities: Create a new Linear project with a name and one or more teams.
Set project metadata at creation: description, lead, status, start date, target date, and priority.
Update an existing project selected by UUID or by partial, case-insensitive name match.
Change a project lead, or remove the lead by passing the value none.
Return machine-readable JSON output with the --json flag for use in scripts.
Resolve team and user names automatically through the official Linear SDK.
limitations: Requires a valid LINEAR_API_KEY and the bun runtime installed on the machine.
Covers project create and update only; it does not manage issues, cycles, or comments.
Partial name matching may select the wrong project when several names are similar.

use_cases.title: Kick off a new initiative
use_cases.description: A team lead creates a new project for an upcoming initiative, assigning it to the correct teams and setting the lead and target date in one command.

use_cases.title: Automate project setup in scripts
use_cases.description: A developer adds project creation to a provisioning script so that each new client engagement gets a standard Linear project without manual clicks.

use_cases.title: Bulk status and date updates
use_cases.description: An operations manager updates the status and target dates of several projects at the end of a planning cycle from a shell loop instead of the web app.

prompt_templates.title: Create a simple project
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a new Linear project named "Website Redesign" for the Engineering team.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: a single project with one team.

prompt_templates.title: Create a project with details
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Linear project named "Q1 Launch" for the Engineering and Product teams, with a target date of 2025-03-01 and priority high.

prompt_templates.title: Update an existing project
prompt_templates.prompt: Update the Linear project named "Website Redesign" to set its status to completed.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: change one field on an existing project.

prompt_templates.title: Reassign lead and get JSON output
prompt_templates.prompt: Update the Linear project "Q1 Launch" to set the lead to "James Monroe" and a new target date of 2025-04-15, and return the result as JSON so I can log it.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: multiple field changes with machine-readable output for automation.

output_examples.input: Create a new Linear project named "Website Redesign" for the Engineering team.
output_examples.output: Created project "Website Redesign" assigned to the Engineering team. The project is set to the planned status and has no lead or target date yet.

output_examples.input: Update the Linear project named "Website Redesign" to set its status to completed.
output_examples.output: Updated project "Website Redesign". Its status is now completed. No other fields were changed.

best_practices: Store the LINEAR_API_KEY in a git-ignored .env file or the environment so it is never committed to source control.
Prefer the project UUID over a name when updating in scripts, because names can match more than one project.
Use the --json flag when the output feeds another program, and read the fields you need from the returned data.
anti_patterns: Do not paste the API key directly into commands or commit it to a shared repository.
Do not rely on a short partial name match for a critical update, since it may select the wrong project.
Do not expect this skill to manage issues, cycles, or comments; it handles projects only.

faq.question: What do I need before I can use this skill?
faq.answer: You need the bun runtime installed and a LINEAR_API_KEY set in your environment or in a .env file at the git root. You can create the key in Linear under Settings, API, Personal API keys.

faq.question: Can I assign a project to more than one team?
faq.answer: Yes. Pass a comma-separated list of team names, for example "Engineering,Product", when you create the project.

faq.question: How do I select the project I want to update?
faq.answer: You can pass the project UUID or a project name. Name matching is partial and case-insensitive, so use a UUID when you need an exact match.

faq.question: How do I remove a project lead?
faq.answer: Set the lead value to the word none when you update the project. This clears the current lead.

faq.question: Can I get output that a script can read?
faq.answer: Yes. Add the --json flag to any command and the tool returns machine-readable JSON instead of plain text.

faq.question: Can this skill delete a Linear project?
faq.answer: No. This skill only creates and updates projects. It does not delete or archive them, and it does not manage issues or comments.
